title: TP stability: add collectives + scheduler health dashboard panels and alert rules (watchdog/quarantine)
author: Sergio Costa
description: Context: We’ve had multiple incidents where TP groups enter a stuck/no-forward-progress state under sustained load, but oncall couldn’t quickly separate “comm stall” vs “kernel stall” vs “scheduler starvation”. This PR extends the TP Collectives + Scheduler Health dashboard and adds alert rules targeted at the new runtime signals landing in runtime 1.19 (watchdog/quarantine + collective latency histograms + TP-group resets). Goal: reduce MTTD and provide actionable links to the runbook/playbook during incidents. What’s in this PR: (1) Grafana dashboard updates: new panels for collective latency (p50/p95/p99) by collective op + model + GPU type, per-TP-group forward progress counters, watchdog triggers (rate + last-seen), quarantine state counts, and TP-group reset counts with correlation panels against 5xx/timeouts. Includes a “stalls triage” row with quick filters (cluster, pool, model, tp_degree) and a small panel that highlights top 10 TP groups by “no progress seconds”. (2) Alert rules: added 4 alert rules with multi-window tuning to avoid paging on transient spikes: TPCollectiveLatencyP99High (warn+page), TPWatchdogTriggersHigh (page), TPGroupResetLoop (page), and TPGroupQuarantineSustained (warn). All alerts include labels (cluster, pool, model, tp_degree) and link to the oncall runbook section “TP hangs / TP watchdog”. (3) Runbook links + annotations: dashboard now has a top-level annotation row referencing the Debugging TP Hangs playbook and the TP group watchdog/quarantine initiative doc, and alert annotations point to the “Immediate mitigations” section (traffic shift, disable TP, adjust timeout knobs) while we’re still in staged rollout. Metrics expected (runtime 1.19+): This PR assumes the following Prometheus series exist (names aligned with runtime PRs ENG-2404/2407): redwood_runtime_tp_collective_latency_seconds_bucket{collective=...,model=...,tp_degree=...,pool=...}; redwood_runtime_tp_watchdog_trigger_total{reason=...,pool=...,cluster=...}; redwood_runtime_tp_group_reset_total{cause=...,pool=...,cluster=...}; redwood_runtime_tp_group_quarantined{pool=...,cluster=...}; redwood_runtime_tp_rank_progress_tokens_total{rank=...,tp_group=...,pool=...,cluster=...}. If any naming changes are needed before runtime 1.19 GA, we can follow up with a quick patch here; I tried to keep the queries tolerant via regex selectors and fallback panels where possible. Alert details (high level): TPCollectiveLatencyP99High triggers when p99 of any collective exceeds 2.5s for 10m (warn) and 5.0s for 10m (page) for pools tagged tp_enabled=true. TPWatchdogTriggersHigh pages when watchdog triggers > 2 per minute for 10m in a pool/cluster (this catches “group stuck and being quarantined repeatedly”). TPGroupResetLoop pages when resets for a pool exceed 10 in 15m AND error rate (5xx or request_timeout) is elevated (basic correlation guard to reduce noise during controlled rollouts). TPGroupQuarantineSustained warns when quarantined group count is nonzero for > 20m in a pool (useful early signal without paging). Screenshots: See attached in the PR (Grafana export preview) for the updated “TP Collectives and Scheduler Health” dashboard; I also included a before/after diff of the main row ordering to make it easier for oncall to find the critical panels. Rollout: This is safe to merge now; panels will show as empty until runtime 1.19 metrics are present. For Hosted canary pools, SRE can enable paging routes for the new alerts once runtime deploy is in the canary stage; until then, alerts are defaulted to ‘disabled’ in prod folders, but available in ‘staging/perf-canary’ for validation. Testing: validated dashboard JSON imports into staging Grafana; promtool rule lint passes; verified alerts fire in a synthetic replay by injecting metric series in the dev Prometheus sandbox. Follow-ups: (a) once runtime PR-18470 logs/spans are fully rolled out, we should add a panel linking trace exemplars for the “collective stall suspected” series; (b) consider splitting out a dedicated “TP watchdog” dashboard if oncall finds the combined dashboard too dense during incidents.
commits: 1) dashboards: add TP collective latency panels + group health summary 2) alerts: introduce watchdog + reset loop rules w/ runbook annotations 3) dashboards: add correlation row vs 5xx/timeouts and top offenders 4) chore: align folder structure + add templating variables (cluster/pool/model) 5) docs: add dashboard README blurb + runbook links
ci_checks: build: pass; lint: pass; promtool: pass; grafana-jsonnet-render: pass; unit (pack validation): pass
review_conversation: Allison Grant: The dashboard looks good, but can we standardize legend formatting? The p99 panel currently mixes model + pool; oncall typically wants pool first. Also please add an annotation linking to the runbook section directly (deep link). Sergio Costa: Updated legends to `pool / model / collective` and moved pool to the front; added deep link to Confluence anchor in both dashboard description and alert annotations. Aisha Bello: Alert thresholds: 5s p99 for collectives seems high/low depending on pool. Do we need different defaults for Dedicated vs Hosted? Rafael mentioned different watchdog sensitivity experiments. Sergio Costa: Agreed; I kept rules generic but scoped to tp_enabled pools and set paging to disabled by default in prod folders. Added comments for SRE to tune per folder, and added a `deployment_mode` label hook if/when we propagate it. Rafael Mendes: Please ensure we don’t page on perf-canary noise. Can we require elevated timeout rate for the reset loop page? Sergio Costa: Added correlation guard (reset loop requires elevated timeout/5xx) and increased the window to 15m with 2-of-3 evaluation to reduce flapping. Tomáš Novák: Runbook link should go to the oncall doc in the oncall folder, not the engineering playbook. Also add a short “Immediate mitigations” panel note. Sergio Costa: Updated links to the oncall readiness doc as primary and the debugging playbook as secondary; added a note block with mitigations and pointers (traffic shift, disable TP, increase collective timeout knob only as temporary). Omar El-Sayed: Query nit: for `*_bucket` please use `histogram_quantile` with `sum by (le, pool, model, collective)`; current query was missing `collective` in one panel. Sergio Costa: Fixed aggregation and added a unit check in the jsonnet render test.
release_notes: Observability pack: adds TP collectives latency panels, watchdog/quarantine panels, and new alert rules for TP watchdog triggers and TP-group reset loops with direct runbook links (intended for runtime 1.19+).
